title: Fit and cure a gel nail extension
instruction: Seat the prepared clear extension on the practice nail, cure the gel, and leave the extension secure with both hands clear. Keep gel off the surrounding skin.
context: Gel nail extensions are a familiar manicure procedure. The curved surfaces must mate without lifted areas, then remain aligned while the adhesive cures.
setup: Clamped 70 × 22 × 20 mm silicone practice finger has a 14 × 12 mm ABS nail insert with 14 mm transverse curvature. A matching 28 × 10–14 mm clear extension holds 0.04 ± 0.01 mL of compatible gel, with its distal 8 mm dry. It starts separate on a wooden support beside a 66 × 58 × 47 mm Kiara Sky Flash Cure lamp. The lamp has a 20 mm spacer; all equipment stands on a 65 mm riser. Both grippers have 45 × 4 mm steel extensions with silicone faces. README specifies preparation and fixed coordinates.
scoring: After at least 40 seconds of exposed cure and 3 seconds with both hands clear, apply a 1 N outward load through a central pull tab for 3 seconds, ramping on and off over 0.5 seconds. More than 1 mm lifting/slip, gel on surrounding skin, damage, edge misalignment above 1.5 mm, tilt above 8°, or an incomplete cure/proof scores 0. Otherwise, judge the visible bonded area with a 1 mm grid: ≥90% earns 1.0; ≥75% earns 0.5; ≥50% earns 0.25; less earns 0. Held results score 0.
fidelity: A curved rigid tip contacts 35 prepared gel patches; a 0.15 mm margin approximates gel bridging across mesh gaps. Exposure creates finite native bonds, tested by a released 1 N central pull. Gel flow, chemical conversion, individual bubbles and tip fracture are omitted. Unseated regions stay unbonded; spills and bond failure remain possible. Material parameters are uncalibrated. A finite native grip approximates friction and transmits reaction loads. No person is used.
scores: Demo: 1.0 (2,180 actions). Dream-1: 0.0 (2,400 actions; session diagnostics in README).
